# Three Blocks Pro - Complete API Documentation

> Worker-based physics engine for Three.js WebGPU

This file contains the complete API reference for Three Blocks Pro.
For a lightweight navigation index, see: https://threejs-blocks.com/pro/llms.txt

## Installation

```bash
npm install @three-blocks/pro
```

```js
import * as THREE from 'three/webgpu';
import { Physics, PhysicsController, BodyType, syncPhysics } from '@three-blocks/pro';
```

## Quick Start

```js
// Initialize physics
const physics = new Physics();
await physics.init();

await physics.addBody(BodyType.STATIC, groundMesh, { friction: 1 });
await physics.addBody(BodyType.DYNAMIC, playerMesh, { mass: 1.5 }, {
  capsuleRadius: 0.5,
  capsuleLength: 1,
  initialPosition: [0, 5, 0]
});

await physics.start();
const controller = new PhysicsController( physics );

function animate( delta ) {
  controller.update( delta );
  const alpha = controller.getInterpolationAlpha();
  syncPhysics( physics.player, playerMesh, alpha );
  renderer.render( scene, camera );
}
```

## LLM Guide

Purpose: help LLMs generate correct integrations for the Three Blocks Pro
worker-based physics engine.

## Requirements (must-haves)

- Three.js r182+ with WebGPU (`three/webgpu`).
- SharedArrayBuffer enabled via COOP/COEP headers:
  - `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`
  - `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`
- HTTPS origin (or localhost) so SharedArrayBuffer works.
- Use `Physics.isSupported()` to fail fast in unsupported browsers.

## Canonical setup order (do this sequence)

1. Create `Physics` with config (gravity, physicsModel, limits).
2. `await physics.init()` before adding bodies.
3. Add bodies via `addBody(BodyType, mesh, options, capsuleOptions)`.
4. `await physics.start()` to begin the worker loop.
5. In the render loop, update controller/input, then call `body.sync(alpha)` on bodies.

```js
import * as THREE from 'three/webgpu';
import {
  Physics,
  PhysicsController,
  BodyType,
} from '@three-blocks/pro';

const physics = new Physics({ gravity: -9.81, physicsModel: 'arcade' });
await physics.init();

await physics.addBody(BodyType.STATIC, groundMesh, { friction: 1 });

// Position the mesh before adding physics
playerMesh.position.set(0, 5, 0);
const playerApi = await physics.addBody(BodyType.DYNAMIC, playerMesh, { mass: 1.5, friction: 0.3 }, {
  capsuleRadius: 0.5,
  capsuleLength: 1,
});
const playerBody = playerApi.body;

await physics.start();

// IMPORTANT: playerBodyIndex must match the dynamic body index (usually 0)
const controller = new PhysicsController(physics, {
  enableInput: true,
  playerBodyIndex: 0,
});

function animate(delta) {
  controller.update(delta);
  const alpha = controller.getInterpolationAlpha();
  playerBody.sync(alpha);  // Syncs physics state to mesh with interpolation
  renderer.render(scene, camera);
  requestAnimationFrame(animate);
}
```

## Frame loop patterns

### Recommended: PhysicsController + body.sync()

- `controller.update(delta)` handles interpolation and input state.
- Use `controller.getInterpolationAlpha()` to smooth between physics steps.
- Call `body.sync(alpha)` on all visible bodies (works for regular meshes and BatchedMesh/InstancedMesh).

### Direct state read (advanced)

- Use the body reference stored from `addBody()`:
  - `api.body.view` for direct buffer-backed object access (zero-copy).
  - `api.body.position` / `api.body.quaternion` for Three.js-like interface.
  - `physics.cameraState` for camera data.
- Write inputs via `physics.bindInput()` / `physics.updateInput()` or use temp
  buffers if you know the schema.

## Input handling

- Use `InputController` or let `PhysicsController` create one:
  - `new PhysicsController(physics, { enableInput: true })`
  - Access via `controller.input` (when enabled).
- If you bind inputs manually:
  - `physics.bindInput(inputController, { playerIndex: 0, jumpVelocity: 8 })`
  - Call `physics.updateInput()` each frame before physics update.

## Body types (use BodyType enum)

- `STATIC`: world geometry. Use `addBody(BodyType.STATIC, mesh, { friction })`.
- `DYNAMIC`: player/character capsule with full physics.
- `KINEMATIC`: moving platforms, NPCs, AI bots. Move via body API (see below).
- `ZONE`: trigger volume. No collision response, just enter/leave events.

## BatchedMesh Support (IMPORTANT)

For high-performance scenarios with many dynamic bodies, use `THREE.BatchedMesh` directly with the physics system. This enables single draw call rendering while maintaining full physics simulation.

### Using BatchedMesh with addBodies

Pass the BatchedMesh with `options.instanceMatrixIndex` and `options.sourceGeometry` in the body config:

```js
// Create BatchedMesh with geometries (non-indexed for consistency)
const boxGeom = new THREE.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 1);
const sphereGeom = new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.5);

const batchedMesh = new THREE.BatchedMesh(maxCount, maxVertices, 0, material);
const boxGeoId = batchedMesh.addGeometry(boxGeom.toNonIndexed());
const sphereGeoId = batchedMesh.addGeometry(sphereGeom.toNonIndexed());
scene.add(batchedMesh);

// Keep original geometries for physics collision shapes
const sourceGeometries = [boxGeom, sphereGeom];

// Add instances and physics bodies
const bodiesConfig = [];
for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
  const geoIndex = i % 2;
  const geometryId = geoIndex === 0 ? boxGeoId : sphereGeoId;
  const instanceId = batchedMesh.addInstance(geometryId);

  // Set initial transform
  matrix.compose(position, quaternion, scale);
  batchedMesh.setMatrixAt(instanceId, matrix);
  batchedMesh.setColorAt(instanceId, color);

  bodiesConfig.push({
    mesh: batchedMesh,
    properties: {
      mass: 1.0,
      friction: 0.5,
      collisionType: BodyCollisionType.BOX,
    },
    bodyProps: {
      initialPosition: [x, y, z],              // Required for dynamic: mesh container is at origin
      initialQuaternion: [qx, qy, qz, qw],     // Required if rotated: mesh rotation not extracted
    },
    options: {
      instanceMatrixIndex: instanceId,         // Required: which instance this body controls
      sourceGeometry: sourceGeometries[geoIndex], // Required: geometry for collision shape
    },
  });
}

const apis = await physics.addBodies(BodyType.DYNAMIC, bodiesConfig);
```

### Syncing BatchedMesh in Animation Loop

Use `body.sync(alpha)` - it works automatically for BatchedMesh/InstancedMesh:

```js
// In animation loop
const alpha = controller.getInterpolationAlpha();
for (const api of dynamicBodyApis) {
  api.body.sync(alpha);  // Handles BatchedMesh matrix composition internally
}
```

The `body.sync()` method automatically:
- Stores instance index and scale at body creation
- Composes matrices with interpolated position/quaternion
- Calls `batchedMesh.setMatrixAt()` for you

For advanced scenarios (e.g., sleep-state colors), you can still access raw state:

```js
// Store instance data for syncing
const instanceData = apis.map((api, i) => ({
  instanceId: bodiesConfig[i].instanceId,
  bodyApi: api,
  scale: scales[i],  // Store scale since physics doesn't track it
}));

// In animation loop
const alpha = controller.getInterpolationAlpha();
for (const data of instanceData) {
  const state = physics.getDynamicBody(data.bodyApi.index);
  if (state) {
    // Property names: positionx/y/z, prevPositionx/y/z, quaternionx/y/z/w, prevQuaternionx/y/z/w
    // Interpolate position
    _position.set(
      state.prevPositionx + (state.positionx - state.prevPositionx) * alpha,
      state.prevPositiony + (state.positiony - state.prevPositiony) * alpha,
      state.prevPositionz + (state.positionz - state.prevPositionz) * alpha
    );

    // Interpolate quaternion
    _quaternion.set(state.prevQuaternionx, state.prevQuaterniony, state.prevQuaternionz, state.prevQuaternionw);
    const targetQuat = new THREE.Quaternion(state.quaternionx, state.quaterniony, state.quaternionz, state.quaternionw);
    _quaternion.slerp(targetQuat, alpha);

    // Use stored scale (physics doesn't track scale)
    _scale.setScalar(data.scale);

    // Compose and set matrix
    _matrix.compose(_position, _quaternion, _scale);
    batchedMesh.setMatrixAt(data.instanceId, _matrix);
  }
}
```

### BatchedMesh Common Mistakes

- **Missing sourceGeometry** - Physics cannot extract geometry from BatchedMesh automatically. You MUST provide `options.sourceGeometry` for collision shape creation.
- **Missing initialPosition for dynamic bodies** - The BatchedMesh container is typically at origin, so position extraction fails. You MUST provide `bodyProps.initialPosition: [x, y, z]` for dynamic/kinematic bodies.
- **Wrong property names** - Use `options.instanceMatrixIndex` (not `instanceId`). The config structure is `{ mesh, properties, bodyProps, options: { instanceMatrixIndex, sourceGeometry } }`.
- **Inconsistent geometry indices** - All geometries in BatchedMesh must be either all indexed or all non-indexed. Use `.toNonIndexed()` on all geometries for consistency.
- **Creating proxy meshes** - Do NOT create individual meshes for physics. Pass `mesh: batchedMesh` directly.
- **Manual matrix composition** - Use `body.sync(alpha)` instead of manual matrix composition - it handles BatchedMesh automatically.
- **Not storing scale** - Physics doesn't track scale. Store it per-instance and apply during matrix composition.
- **Not calling setVisibleAt()** - New BatchedMesh instances may default to invisible. Call `batchedMesh.setVisibleAt(instanceId, true)` after adding.

## Dynamic ↔ Dynamic Collision (IMPORTANT)

Dynamic bodies can collide with each other using BVH-based collision detection. The system automatically selects the optimal collision mode based on geometry, or you can specify it explicitly.

### Collision Modes (BodyCollisionType)

| Mode | Complexity | Best For |
|------|------------|----------|
| `SPHERE` | O(1) | SphereGeometry, IcosahedronGeometry |
| `CAPSULE` | O(1) | CapsuleGeometry, CylinderGeometry |
| `BOX` | O(log n) | BoxGeometry, most convex shapes |
| `FULL` | O(log n × log m) | Concave shapes (TorusKnot, etc.) |
| `FULL_PRECISE` | O(n log n) | When exact contact points needed |

```js
import { BodyCollisionType } from '@three-blocks/pro';

// Explicit collision type
const api = await physics.addBody(BodyType.DYNAMIC, torusMesh, {
  mass: 1.0,
  collisionType: BodyCollisionType.FULL,
});

// Auto-detect from geometry (default)
const api2 = await physics.addBody(BodyType.DYNAMIC, boxMesh, { mass: 1.0 });

// Runtime change
api.body.collisionType = BodyCollisionType.BOX;

// Disable D↔D collision for performance
api.body.collidesWithDynamic = false;
```

### Collision Response Models

The engine uses pluggable response models via `CollisionResponseRegistry`:

```js
import { collisionResponseRegistry, MomentumTransferResponse } from '@three-blocks/pro';

// Use momentum-based response (bouncy)
collisionResponseRegistry.register(MomentumTransferResponse);
collisionResponseRegistry.setActiveModel('momentum-transfer');

// Or use SimplePushResponse (default, equal push apart)
collisionResponseRegistry.setActiveModel('simple-push');
```

### Custom Response Model

```js
const BouncyResponse = {
  name: 'bouncy',
  config: { restitution: 0.8, positionCorrection: 1.0 },

  resolve(bodyA, bodyB, normal, penetration) {
    // normal points A→B (A moves -normal, B moves +normal)
    const half = penetration * 0.5;
    bodyA.position.addScaledVector(normal, -half);
    bodyB.position.addScaledVector(normal, half);
    // Add velocity impulse for bounce...
  },
};

collisionResponseRegistry.register(BouncyResponse);
```

**Critical:** Normal direction must point from A toward B. Wrong direction causes oscillation.

## Driving Bodies on Dynamic Bodies (Character Controller on Physics Objects)

When a character controller (driving body) stands on a dynamic physics object (like a pushable box), the engine uses a **Ride/Push pattern** based on contact normal to ensure stability.

### Driving vs Non-Driving Bodies

| Type | Flag | Behavior |
|------|------|----------|
| **Driving** | `driving: true` | Character controller with player input, uses groundMove/airMove physics |
| **Non-Driving** | `driving: false` | Physics object with gravity and impulse response |

By default, dynamic bodies added via `addBody(BodyType.DYNAMIC, ...)` are **driving** (character controllers). To create a physics object (pushable box), set `driving: false`:

```js
// Character controller (driving) - default
const playerApi = await physics.addBody(BodyType.DYNAMIC, playerMesh, { mass: 1.5 });

// Physics object (non-driving) - pushable box
const boxApi = await physics.addBody(BodyType.DYNAMIC, boxMesh, {
  mass: 1.0,
  driving: false,  // Important: makes this a physics object, not a character
});
```

### Ride/Push Pattern

The collision response between a driving body and a non-driving dynamic body depends on the **contact normal direction**:

| Contact Type | Detection | Behavior |
|--------------|-----------|----------|
| Standing on top | `ny < -0.7` | **Ride pattern**: Player follows box, marked as grounded |
| Side collision | `ny >= -0.7` | **Push pattern**: Mass-weighted correction, box gets pushed |

#### Ride Pattern (Standing on Dynamic Body)

When player stands ON TOP of a dynamic box:
1. Player position corrected UPWARD (resolve penetration by lifting player)
2. Box receives NO position correction (ground supports it)
3. Player marked as grounded (`groundAngle = 0`) - groundMove physics apply
4. Player velocity matched to box velocity (ride together)

```js
// Player standing on box: stable, recognized as grounded
// - Player can walk, jump normally
// - Box remains stable (no shaking from collision fighting)
// - If box moves, player rides along
```

#### Push Pattern (Side Collision)

When player collides with dynamic box from the side:
1. Mass-weighted position correction (lighter body moves more)
2. Box gets pushed away from player
3. Standard physics response

```js
// Player walks into side of box: box gets pushed
// - Player loses some momentum
// - Box moves away from player
// - No instability or shaking
```

### Common Issues This Solves

| Issue | Cause | Solution (Ride/Push Pattern) |
|-------|-------|------------------------------|
| Box shakes when player stands on it | Collision impulse fighting (player down, ground up) | Ride pattern: no downward impulse on box |
| Player velocity accumulates infinitely | Gravity applied but not zeroed | Ride pattern: velocity matched to box |
| Player not recognized as grounded | groundAngle not set | Ride pattern: sets `groundAngle = 0` |
| Player pushed through box | Collision response instability | Ride pattern: stable position correction |

### Testing Driving + Dynamic Interactions

```js
// Create a scene with player standing on dynamic box
const playerApi = await physics.addBody(BodyType.DYNAMIC, playerMesh, { mass: 1.5 });
const boxApi = await physics.addBody(BodyType.DYNAMIC, boxMesh, {
  mass: 2.0,
  driving: false,  // Physics object
});

// Expected behavior:
// 1. Player can walk onto box and stand stable
// 2. Player is recognized as grounded (can jump)
// 3. Box doesn't shake or become unstable
// 4. Pushing box from side: box moves, player can follow
```

## Angular Velocity & Rotation Physics (NEW)

Enable realistic rotation response during collisions. When enabled, objects spin and roll based on collision impulses and surface friction.

### Enabling Rotation Response

```js
// Enable when creating body
const api = await physics.addBody(BodyType.DYNAMIC, mesh, {
  mass: 1.0,
  friction: 0.5,
  enableRotationResponse: true,  // Enable angular velocity from collisions
  angularDamping: 0.1,           // Damping factor (0-1, default 0.1)
});

// Or toggle at runtime
api.body.enableRotationResponse = true;
api.body.angularDamping = 0.05;  // Lower = spins longer
```

### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `enableRotationResponse` | boolean | Enable/disable rotation physics (default: false) |
| `angularDamping` | number | Rotation slowdown factor 0-1 (default: 0.1) |
| `angularVelocity` | {x,y,z} | Current angular velocity in radians/sec |
| `momentOfInertia` | number | Auto-calculated from mass and shape |

### Direct Angular Velocity Control

```js
// Set angular velocity directly
api.body.angularVelocity.set(0, 2, 0);  // Spin around Y axis

// Read current values
const omega = api.body.angularVelocity.toVector3();
console.log('Spinning at:', omega.length(), 'rad/s');
```

### How It Works

1. **D↔D Collisions**: Angular impulse calculated from torque = r × F (contact offset × impulse)
2. **Ground/Wall Contact**: Rolling torque from friction at contact point
3. **Integration**: Quaternion updated each physics step: q' = q + 0.5 * dt * ω × q
4. **Damping**: Angular velocity reduced each frame by `angularDamping * dt`

### Performance Note

Rotation response is **opt-in** and disabled by default for performance. Only enable on bodies that need realistic rolling/spinning behavior.

## Collision Response Mode

Controls how bodies respond to surface collisions with static/kinematic geometry.

```js
import { CollisionResponseMode } from '@three-blocks/pro';

// Set during body creation
const { body } = await physics.addBody(BodyType.DYNAMIC, playerMesh, {
  mass: 70,
  collisionResponseMode: CollisionResponseMode.ARCADE,  // For arcade movement
});

// Or modify at runtime
body.collisionResponseMode = CollisionResponseMode.REALISTIC;
```

### Modes

| Mode | Value | Behavior |
|------|-------|----------|
| `REALISTIC` | 1 | Only clips velocity on walkable ground. Standard physics (default). |
| `ARCADE` | 0 | Clips velocity against ALL surfaces. Enables sliding on steep ramps. |

### Use Cases

- **REALISTIC (default)**: Player controllers, physics objects, projectiles - standard game physics
- **ARCADE**: Ramp sliding, classic FPS-style movement mechanics

### Example: Arcade Movement

```js
import { CollisionResponseMode } from '@three-blocks/pro';

// Player with arcade-style movement
const { body } = await physics.addBody(BodyType.DYNAMIC, playerMesh, {
  mass: 70,
  friction: 0.3,
  collisionResponseMode: CollisionResponseMode.ARCADE,
});
```

## addBody options (CRITICAL)

The `addBody` function signature is:
```js
await physics.addBody(bodyType, mesh, physicsOptions?, capsuleOptions?)
```

### physicsOptions (3rd parameter)
```js
import { CollisionResponseMode } from '@three-blocks/pro';

{
  mass: 1.5,                      // For DYNAMIC bodies
  friction: 0.3,                  // Surface friction
  enableRotationResponse: false,  // Enable angular velocity physics (default: false)
  angularDamping: 0.1,            // Rotation damping factor (default: 0.1)
  collisionResponseMode: CollisionResponseMode.REALISTIC,  // Surface collision behavior (default)
}
```

### capsuleOptions (4th parameter) - REQUIRED for DYNAMIC and KINEMATIC
```js
{
  capsuleRadius: 0.5,           // Collision capsule radius
  capsuleLength: 1.0,           // Collision capsule length (height minus caps)
  // Position is automatically extracted from mesh.getWorldPosition()
}
```

> **NOTE:** Position and rotation are automatically extracted from the mesh's world transform
> using `mesh.getWorldPosition()` and `mesh.getWorldQuaternion()`. Simply position your mesh
> in the scene before calling `addBody()`.

### Examples

**Player (DYNAMIC):**
```js
// Position the mesh first
playerMesh.position.set(0, 2, 0);

await physics.addBody(BodyType.DYNAMIC, playerMesh, {
  mass: 1.5,
  friction: 0.3,
}, {
  capsuleRadius: 0.5,
  capsuleLength: 1.0,
});
```

**AI Bot (KINEMATIC):**
```js
// Position the mesh first
botMesh.position.copy(spawnPosition);

await physics.addBody(BodyType.KINEMATIC, botMesh, {
  friction: 0.5,
}, {
  capsuleRadius: 0.4,
  capsuleLength: 0.8,
});
```

**Ground (STATIC):**
```js
// Static bodies don't need capsuleOptions
await physics.addBody(BodyType.STATIC, groundMesh, { friction: 1.0 });
```

### Moving kinematic bodies (IMPORTANT)

```js
// Add kinematic body and store the API
const bodyApi = await physics.addBody(BodyType.KINEMATIC, mesh);

// Move via the body.position API each frame (updates BOTH buffer AND mesh)
bodyApi.body.position.set(x, y, z);
bodyApi.body.quaternion.set(qx, qy, qz, qw);

// Note: position.set() automatically updates the mesh - no sync() call needed for kinematic!
```

> **CRITICAL:** Use `body.position.set(x, y, z)` - NOT `body.setPosition(x, y, z)`.
> The Body class has a `position` property with `.set()`, `.x`, `.y`, `.z` methods.
> There is NO `setPosition()` method on Body.

> **WARNING:** Do NOT use non-existent methods like:
> - `body.setPosition()` - WRONG, does not exist
> - `physics.setKinematicPosition()` - WRONG, does not exist
> - `physics.api.setKinematicTransform()` - WRONG, does not exist

### Removing bodies

Bodies can be removed at runtime using `removeBody()` or `removeBodies()`:

```js
// Remove using the API object from addBody()
const api = await physics.addBody(BodyType.DYNAMIC, mesh, { mass: 1 });
await physics.removeBody(api);

// Remove using the Body instance
await physics.removeBody(api.body);

// Remove using index and type
await physics.removeBody(5, 'kinematic');

// Remove multiple bodies at once
const apis = await physics.addBodies(BodyType.KINEMATIC, configs);
await physics.removeBodies(apis);
```

**Important:** After removing a body:
- The body slot is freed and can be reused by new bodies
- Event listeners are automatically detached
- The mesh's `userData._physicsBody` reference is cleared
- You must remove the mesh from the scene separately if desired

> **WARNING:** Do NOT use non-existent methods like `physics.setKinematicPosition()`
> or `physics.api.setKinematicTransform()`. These do not exist!

### Teleporting bodies

Use `teleportBody()` to instantly reposition a dynamic body (e.g., respawn player):

```js
import { teleportBody } from '@three-blocks/pro';

// Teleport to position [x, y, z]
teleportBody([0, 5, 0]);

// Teleport with rotation (quaternion [x, y, z, w])
teleportBody([0, 5, 0], [0, 0, 0, 1]);

// Teleport specific body by index (default: 0 = player)
teleportBody([10, 2, 10], null, 1);  // Body index 1
```

**What teleportBody does:**
- Updates physics state atomically via worker
- Updates visual mesh immediately for instant feedback
- Handles camera state for smooth transition (disables lerp briefly)
- Resets camera rotation if quaternion provided (non-lockRotation mode)

**Example: Respawn player**
```js
const spawnPosition = new THREE.Vector3(-6, 2, 0);

function respawnPlayer() {
  teleportBody(spawnPosition.toArray());
}
```

> **Note:** `teleportBody()` works with the driving body (player controller). For other bodies, use `body.position.set(x, y, z)` directly.

## Camera systems

- `FirstPersonCamera` extends `THREE.PerspectiveCamera` and handles pointer
  lock and body rotation internally. Do not pass look input into
  `controller.applyInput()` when using it.
- `ThirdPersonCamera` provides orbit-style follow (if available in your build).
- Low-level option: read `physics.cameraState` and apply to any camera.

## Physics models (movement feel)

- Use built-ins: `'default'`, `'platformer'`, `'realistic'`, `'arcade'`.
- For custom feel, pass `customPhysicsModel` and set `physicsModel` to its name.
- Prefer `extendPreset` / `scalePreset` / `combinePresets` for tweaks.

## Speculative Contacts (RAPIER-style physics)

Enable speculative contacts for stable resting bodies (no Y-velocity oscillation):

```js
// Enable speculative contacts
await physics.setSpeculativeContacts(true);

// Or via physics model config
await physics.api.updatePhysicsModelConfig({
  speculativeContacts: true,
  speculativeMargin: 0.01,      // Prediction margin (default: 0.01)
  speculativeIterations: 8,     // Solver iterations (default: 8)
});
```

**How it works:**
- Standard physics: Gravity applied as `velocity.y -= gravity * dt` → causes oscillation
- Speculative: Gravity applied as constraint bias → ground contacts cancel gravity automatically

**When to use:**
- Bodies that need to rest stably on surfaces (boxes, physics objects)
- Stacking scenarios where oscillation is visible
- Games requiring RAPIER-style stability

**When NOT to use:**
- Character controllers (they have their own ground stabilization)
- When you need the standard gravity-first pipeline

## Navigation & Pathfinding (IMPORTANT)

Bodies can navigate using `body.navigation` API. Two modes available:
- **BASIC**: Straight-line movement, no grid needed
- **ASTAR**: A* pathfinding with obstacle avoidance (requires PathfindingGrid)

### Navigation Types

```js
import { NavigationType } from '@three-blocks/pro';

NavigationType.BASIC   // Straight-line movement (click-to-go)
NavigationType.ASTAR   // A* grid pathfinding
NavigationType.NAVMESH // Navigation mesh (future)
```

### BASIC Navigation (Click-to-Go)

No setup required - just call `navigateTo()`:

```js
// Dynamic body (player) - click-to-go
playerMesh.position.set(0, 2, 0);
const playerApi = await physics.addBody(BodyType.DYNAMIC, playerMesh, {
  mass: 1.5,
}, {
  capsuleRadius: 0.5,
  capsuleLength: 1.0,
});

// Navigate directly (auto-enables BASIC mode)
playerApi.body.navigation.navigateTo(clickPosition);

// Check state
if (playerApi.body.navigation.isNavigating) { ... }

// Stop navigation
playerApi.body.navigation.stop();
```

### A* Pathfinding (AI Bots)

Setup order:
1. Initialize physics and add static bodies
2. Create and compile PathfindingGrid
3. Add kinematic body for bot
4. Enable navigation with grid
5. Start physics
6. Call `navigateTo()`

```js
import { PathfindingGrid, NavigationType } from '@three-blocks/pro';

// 1. Create pathfinding grid
const grid = new PathfindingGrid({
  bounds: new THREE.Box3(
    new THREE.Vector3(-50, 0, -50),
    new THREE.Vector3(50, 10, 50)
  ),
  cellSize: 1.0,
  agentHeight: 1.8,
});

// 2. Initialize and compile grid
await grid.init(physics);
await grid.compile();  // Precomputes walkable areas

// 3. Add kinematic body for bot
botMesh.position.set(10, 1, 10);
const botApi = await physics.addBody(BodyType.KINEMATIC, botMesh, {
  friction: 0.5,
}, {
  capsuleRadius: 0.4,
  capsuleLength: 0.8,
});

// 4. Enable A* navigation with grid
await botApi.body.navigation.enable(grid, {
  maxSpeed: 4.0,             // Movement speed
  arrivalRadius: 1.5,        // Distance to stop at destination
  avoidanceRadius: 1.5,      // Radius for obstacle avoidance
  rotationSpeed: 0.12,       // Turn speed (0-1)
});

// 5. Start physics
await physics.start();

// 6. Navigate to target
botApi.body.navigation.navigateTo(targetPosition);
```

### Common Navigation Mistakes

- **Using deprecated `body.pathfinder`** - Use `body.navigation` instead.
- **Using deprecated `body.enablePathfinding()`** - Use `body.navigation.enable(grid)`.
- **Calling `compile()` before `init()`** - Must call `grid.init(physics)` first.
- **Not syncing kinematic body meshes** - Always sync in the animation loop:
  ```js
  botApi.body.sync(alpha);
  ```

### Body Classes with Navigation

```js
// Check body types (Three.js pattern)
body.isBody          // true for all bodies
body.isDynamicBody   // true for dynamic bodies
body.isKinematicBody // true for kinematic bodies

// Both dynamic and kinematic bodies have navigation
playerApi.body.navigation.navigateTo(target);  // BASIC mode
botApi.body.navigation.navigateTo(target);     // A* mode (if grid enabled)
```

### Navigation with AI System

When using the AI system (Sensors + Intents), navigation is integrated automatically:

```js
import {
  PathfindingGrid, VisionSensor, DamageSensor,
  PatrolIntent, EngageIntent
} from '@three-blocks/pro';

// Create and compile grid
const grid = new PathfindingGrid({ bounds, cellSize: 1.0 });
await grid.init(physics);
await grid.compile();

// Add kinematic body
botMesh.position.copy(spawnPosition);
const botApi = await physics.addBody(BodyType.KINEMATIC, botMesh, {
  friction: 0.5,
}, {
  capsuleRadius: 0.4,
  capsuleLength: 0.8,
});

// Enable A* navigation (required for AI movement)
await botApi.body.navigation.enable(grid, { maxSpeed: 4 });

// Configure AI with sensors and intents
botApi.body.ai
  .addSensor(
    new VisionSensor({ fov: 90, range: 25, targetTypes: ['dynamic'] }),
    new DamageSensor()
  )
  .addIntent(
    new PatrolIntent({ waypoints: [...], priority: 20 }),
    new EngageIntent({ priority: 80, fireRate: 1.5 })
  )
  .enable();
```

## Weapons System

The unified weapons system supports three weapon types:
- **HITSCAN**: Instant raycast (rifles, pistols, lasers)
- **PROJECTILE**: Traveling with physics (arrows, grenades, rockets)
- **HYBRID**: Instant hit + visual projectile (competitive FPS feel)

```js
import { WeaponType, ProjectilePreset } from '@three-blocks/pro';

// Hitscan from camera (FPS crosshair)
weapon.fireFromCamera();

// Hitscan with custom origin/direction (accepts Vector3 or [x,y,z])
weapon.fire(playerApi, {
  origin: muzzlePos,      // Vector3 or [x, y, z]
  direction: aimDir,      // Vector3 or [x, y, z]
});

// Projectile (traveling with physics)
weapon.fire(towerApi, {
  origin: muzzlePos,
  direction: leadDirection,
});

// Hybrid (instant hit + visual projectile)
weapon.fire(playerApi, {
  origin: muzzlePos,
  direction: aimDir,
});

// Convenience methods (using body API directly)
physics.weapons.fireGrenade(playerApi, { direction: throwDir, damage: 100, aoeRadius: 5 });
physics.weapons.fireArrow(towerApi, { direction: aimDir, damage: 30 });
physics.weapons.fireRocket(playerApi, { direction: aimDir, damage: 75 });
```

### Projectile Mesh Syncing (IMPORTANT)

Projectile weapons can have visual meshes that automatically sync with physics. Use `physics.createMeshPool()` to create an InstancedMesh that updates via Three.js `onBeforeRender` callbacks with smooth interpolation.

**Setup Order:**
1. Create mesh template (regular THREE.Mesh)
2. Create mesh pool via `physics.createMeshPool()`
3. Add weapon with the mesh pool
4. Fire weapon - meshes sync automatically

**Basic Example (Rapid-Fire Arrows):**
```js
// 1. Create template mesh
const arrowTemplate = new THREE.Mesh(
  new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.02, 0.02, 0.5, 8),
  new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xcc6600 })
);

// 2. Create InstancedMesh pool (20 simultaneous projectiles max)
const arrowPool = physics.createMeshPool(arrowTemplate, 20, scene);

// 3. Add weapon with mesh pool
const weapon = await physics.addWeapon(WeaponType.PROJECTILE, arrowPool, {
  damage: 35,
  ...ProjectilePreset.ARROW,
});

// 4. Fire weapon - meshes sync automatically
weapon.weapon.fireFromCamera();
```

**Grenade Example (Slow-Firing):**
```js
// Single grenade mesh template
const grenadeTemplate = new THREE.Mesh(
  new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.1, 8, 8),
  new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xff6600 })
);

// Small pool (2 grenades max in flight)
const grenadePool = physics.createMeshPool(grenadeTemplate, 2, scene);

// Add weapon
const grenadeWeapon = await physics.addWeapon(WeaponType.PROJECTILE, grenadePool, {
  damage: 100,
  ...ProjectilePreset.GRENADE,
});

grenadeWeapon.weapon.fireFromCamera();
```

**How It Works:**
- `createMeshPool()` returns a THREE.InstancedMesh with `onBeforeRender` callback attached
- The callback automatically syncs mesh instances with active projectile positions
- Interpolation uses `THREE.MathUtils.lerp()` for smooth rendering between physics updates
- Mesh orientation follows projectile velocity direction
- Instances automatically appear/disappear as projectiles spawn/despawn
- No manual syncing required in your render loop

**Critical Notes:**
- **ALWAYS use `createMeshPool()`** for projectile meshes - do NOT create InstancedMesh manually
- Pool size should match expected max simultaneous projectiles
- Meshes sync automatically via Three.js render lifecycle - no RAF needed
- Interpolation is built-in and always enabled for smooth 120fps+ rendering
- Syncing only occurs when mesh is visible and being rendered (respects renderer state)

### AI with Projectile Weapons

AI automatically leads targets for projectile weapons:

```js
import { EngageIntent, WeaponType } from '@three-blocks/pro';

body.ai.addIntent(new EngageIntent({
  weaponType: WeaponType.PROJECTILE,
  projectileSpeed: 40,  // For auto target leading
  fireRate: 1.0,
  engageRange: 40,
}));
```

### ProjectilePreset Reference

```js
ProjectilePreset.ARROW   // { gravity: 1, drag: 0.01, speed: 40 }
ProjectilePreset.GRENADE // { gravity: 1.5, drag: 0.05, speed: 15, aoeRadius: 5 }
ProjectilePreset.ROCKET  // { gravity: 0.3, drag: 0, speed: 60, aoeRadius: 3 }
ProjectilePreset.MORTAR  // { gravity: 2, drag: 0.02, speed: 25, aoeRadius: 8 }
```

### Accessing Physics Properties

**`physics.gravity`** - Get the current gravity scalar (m/s²):

```js
// Get current gravity value
const gravity = physics.gravity; // -9.81 by default

// Use in trajectory calculations
function calculateTrajectoryPoints(origin, direction, speed) {
  const points = [];
  const dt = 0.05;
  const grenadeGravity = physics.gravity * 1.5; // Grenade preset multiplier
  const drag = 0.05;

  let pos = origin.clone();
  let vel = direction.clone().multiplyScalar(speed);

  for (let i = 0; i < 50; i++) {
    points.push(pos.clone());
    vel.y += grenadeGravity * dt;
    vel.multiplyScalar(1 - drag * dt);
    pos.add(vel.clone().multiplyScalar(dt));
    if (pos.y <= 0) break;
  }

  return points;
}

// Calculate grenade arc
const trajectoryPoints = calculateTrajectoryPoints(
  camera.position,
  cameraDirection,
  15 // ProjectilePreset.GRENADE.speed
);
```

### Projectile Explosion Events

Projectiles automatically emit explosion events when they detonate. Listen globally instead of on individual bodies:

**Subscribe to explosions:**

```js
const unsubscribe = physics.weapons.onExplode((explosion) => {
  console.log(`Explosion at [${explosion.position.x}, ${explosion.position.y}, ${explosion.position.z}]`);
  console.log(`Cause: ${explosion.cause}, Radius: ${explosion.aoeRadius}m`);

  // Spawn visual effects
  spawnExplosionVFX(explosion.position, explosion.aoeRadius);
});

// Cleanup
unsubscribe();
```

**Control detonation behavior:**

```js
// Explode on contact (default for AoE weapons)
grenadeWeapon.fire(playerApi, {
  direction: throwDir,
  explodeOnContact: true,
});

// Delayed detonation (sticky grenade, passes through on contact)
grenadeWeapon.fire(playerApi, {
  direction: throwDir,
  explodeOnContact: false,  // Won't explode until timeout
  lifetime: 2.0,  // 2 second fuse
});
```

**Explosion event data:**
- `position: {x, y, z}` - Detonation location
- `velocity: {x, y, z}` - Projectile velocity at detonation
- `cause: 'collision' | 'timeout'` - What triggered explosion
- `aoeRadius: number` - Blast radius in meters
- `damage: number` - Base damage value
- `targetType/targetIndex` - Hit target (only if cause === 'collision')

## Body Events

Body events use the Three.js EventDispatcher pattern directly on the body:

```js
import { BodyEvent } from '@three-blocks/pro';

// Hit events (all weapon types: hitscan, projectile, hybrid)
api.body.addEventListener(BodyEvent.HIT, (event) => {
  console.log('Hit at:', event.hitPoint, event.hitNormal);
  console.log('Weapon type:', event.weaponType);  // 'hitscan', 'projectile', 'hybrid'
  console.log('Damage:', event.damage);

  // Projectile-specific fields
  if (event.weaponType === 'projectile') {
    console.log('Flight time:', event.flightTime);
  }

  // AoE hits
  if (event.isAoE) {
    console.log('Splash damage from:', event.aoeCenter);
  }
});

// Collision events
api.body.addEventListener(BodyEvent.COLLIDE, (event) => {
  console.log('Collision started');
});
api.body.addEventListener(BodyEvent.COLLIDE_END, () => {
  console.log('Collision ended');
});

// Zone events (on zone bodies)
zoneApi.body.addEventListener(BodyEvent.ZONE_ENTER, () => {
  console.log('Player entered zone');
});
zoneApi.body.addEventListener(BodyEvent.ZONE_LEAVE, () => {
  console.log('Player left zone');
});

// Pointer events
groundApi.body.addEventListener(BodyEvent.POINTER_INTERSECT, (event) => {
  const { colliders, isClick } = event;
  if (isClick && colliders[0]) {
    console.log('Clicked at:', colliders[0].point);
  }
});
```

Available event types:
- `BodyEvent.HIT` - Weapon hit (hitscan, projectile, or hybrid)
- `BodyEvent.COLLIDE` - Collision start
- `BodyEvent.COLLIDE_END` - Collision end
- `BodyEvent.ZONE_ENTER` - Dynamic body entered zone
- `BodyEvent.ZONE_LEAVE` - Dynamic body left zone
- `BodyEvent.POINTER_INTERSECT` - Pointer ray intersection
- `BodyEvent.CAMERA_INTERSECT` - Camera ray intersection

## Interpolation and syncing

- Always use `body.sync(alpha)` for meshes to avoid jitter.
- The `alpha` from `controller.getInterpolationAlpha()` is required for smooth
  render even when physics runs at fixed 60 Hz.

## Debug helpers

- `PhysicsDebug` shows live body state in 3D.
- `PhysicsDebugBVH` renders collision BVH wireframes.

**IMPORTANT:** You must call `.update(renderer)` on debug helpers each frame for them to render:
```js
// In animation loop
physicsDebug.update(renderer);
physicsDebugBVH.update(renderer); // if using BVH debug
renderer.render(scene, camera);
```

## Common pitfalls (LLM checklist)

- Missing COOP/COEP headers => SharedArrayBuffer is undefined.
- Calling `addBody` before `await physics.init()` => buffer views not ready.
- Forgetting `await physics.start()` => worker loop never runs.
- Using `FirstPersonCamera` but still applying "look" input => double rotation.
- Skipping `body.sync()` or interpolation => visible jitter.
- **Forgetting to position mesh before `addBody()`** => Body spawns at origin (0,0,0).
  Always set `mesh.position` before calling `addBody()` - position is automatically
  extracted from the mesh's world transform.
- **Omitting `playerBodyIndex` in PhysicsController** => Controller doesn't know
  which body is the player. Always pass `playerBodyIndex: 0` (or the correct index).
  ```js
  // WRONG - player will fall through ground
  const controller = new PhysicsController(physics);

  // CORRECT
  const controller = new PhysicsController(physics, {
    enableInput: true,
    playerBodyIndex: 0,
  });
  ```
- **Moving kinematic bodies incorrectly** => Use `bodyApi.body.position.set(x, y, z)`.
  The `body.position` is an object with `.set()`, `.x`, `.y`, `.z` methods.
  Common mistakes:
  - `body.setPosition(x, y, z)` - WRONG, does not exist
  - `physics.setKinematicPosition()` - WRONG, does not exist
  - `physics.api.setKinematicTransform()` - WRONG, does not exist
  ```js
  // WRONG - setPosition does not exist
  kinematicBody.setPosition(x, y, z);

  // CORRECT - use position.set()
  kinematicBody.position.set(x, y, z);
  ```
- **Using deprecated `body.pathfinder`** => Use `body.navigation` instead.
- **Using deprecated `body.enablePathfinding()`** => Use `body.navigation.enable(grid)`.
- **Forgetting to compile PathfindingGrid** => Call `await grid.compile()` after `init()`.
- **Wrong collision normal direction** => Normal must point A→B (from bodyA toward bodyB).
  If normal points B→A, bodies will oscillate (attract/repulse in loop) instead of separating.
  Use `normal = centerB - centerA` not `centerA - centerB`.
- **Creating proxy meshes for BatchedMesh** => Do NOT create individual meshes for physics
  when using BatchedMesh. Pass `mesh: batchedMesh` with proper options.
  ```js
  // WRONG - creates unnecessary proxy meshes
  const proxyMesh = new THREE.Mesh(geometry);
  bodiesConfig.push({ mesh: proxyMesh, properties: {...} });

  // CORRECT - pass BatchedMesh with options
  bodiesConfig.push({
    mesh: batchedMesh,
    properties: {...},
    options: {
      instanceMatrixIndex: instanceId,
      sourceGeometry: originalGeometry,
    }
  });
  ```
- **Manual matrix composition for BatchedMesh** => Use `body.sync(alpha)` instead - it handles
  BatchedMesh automatically by storing instance index and scale at body creation.
- **Hiding dead entities without removing physics bodies** => When entities die,
  call `physics.removeBody(api)` to fully remove them. Just hiding the mesh
  (`mesh.visible = false`) leaves the body active in the simulation, causing:
  - PhysicsDebug to still show the body
  - Memory/performance waste
  - Potential collision issues
  ```js
  // WRONG - body still in simulation
  monster.mesh.visible = false;

  // CORRECT - fully removes body
  monster.mesh.visible = false;
  physics.removeBody(monster.api);
  ```
- **Forgetting `physicsDebug.update(renderer)` in animation loop** => Debug visualization won't
  render. Always call `.update(renderer)` each frame:
  ```js
  // In animation loop
  physicsDebug.update(renderer);
  renderer.render(scene, camera);
  ```

## Reading Physics State (Advanced)

### Recommended: Use Body Reference from addBody()

Always store and use the api reference returned from `addBody()`:

```js
// Store the api reference
const playerApi = await physics.addBody(BodyType.DYNAMIC, playerMesh);

// Access body state via api.body
const body = playerApi.body;

// Position/quaternion with Three.js-like interface
body.position.set(0, 10, 0);
body.quaternion.setFromAxisAngle({ x: 0, y: 1, z: 0 }, Math.PI);

// Sync to mesh with interpolation
body.sync(controller.getInterpolationAlpha());

// Direct buffer access via body.view
const view = body.view;
console.log({
  position: [view.positionx, view.positiony, view.positionz],
  velocity: [view.localVelocityx, view.localVelocityy, view.localVelocityz],
  ground: view.ground,
  sleepState: view.sleepState, // 0=awake, 1=drowsy, 2=sleeping
});
```

### Internal APIs (avoid in application code)

These are low-level internal methods - prefer the body reference pattern above:

```js
// Internal - use api.body instead
physics.getView('dynamic')    // Raw buffer views (internal)
physics.getDynamicBody(i)     // Returns view by index (internal)
physics.getKinematicBody(i)   // Returns view by index (internal)
```

### Buffer-Backed Object Properties

Key properties available on `body.view`:
- `positionx/y/z`, `prevPositionx/y/z` - Position and previous (for interpolation)
- `quaternionx/y/z/w`, `prevQuaternionx/y/z/w` - Rotation quaternion
- `localVelocityx/y/z` - Local-space velocity
- `externalVelocityx/y/z` - External velocity (from collisions/platforms)
- `angularVelocityx/y/z` - Angular velocity (rad/s)
- `ground` - Is on ground (0/1)
- `sleepState` - Sleep state (0=awake, 1=drowsy, 2=sleeping)
- `groundAngle`, `surfaceAngle` - Surface angles in radians
